Journal Recovery Example

gxdJournal transactions survive a writer that is killed in the middle of one: Recover() leaves only whole batches.

Contents

What It Shows
Running It
Sample Output
Source

What It Shows

A transaction groups several writes so that after a crash either all of them are in the database file or none are (gxdjrnl.h, new in 7.2). The program proves it by killing a writer in the middle of its work:

  1. A child process opens a journal, creates a gxDatabase file, attaches it to the journal and writes batches of 25 records, one transaction per batch (Begin, Alloc and Write, Commit). After each commit it writes the number of committed batches to a progress file.
  2. The parent waits for a few commits, then kills the child with SIGKILL at a random moment, usually inside a transaction. Nothing in the child gets to clean up.
  3. The parent calls gxdJournal::Recover(), which writes every committed transaction left in the journal to the database file and drops the one that was not committed.
  4. It opens the database and checks it: every record belongs to a whole batch, no batch is partly there, and every batch the child reported is present. One more batch may be there, when the child was killed after Commit() returned and before it wrote the progress file.
  5. Finally it shows Rollback(): a rolled-back insert leaves no trace.

The program uses fork() and kill(), so it is built only on Linux and other POSIX systems.

Running It

journal_recovery [rounds]      # default 5

It writes journal_recovery.gxd, .jnl and .progress in the current folder and exits with 0 when every round recovers to a consistent database.

Sample Output

Round 1: killed after 3 committed batches; Recover() wrote 4 transactions from the journal; database holds 4 whole batches (the last commit beat its progress note) - consistent
Round 2: killed after 6 committed batches; Recover() wrote 6 transactions from the journal; database holds 6 whole batches - consistent
...
Rollback: 200 records before, 200 after a rolled-back insert
Every crash recovered to a consistent database

Source

examples/oodb/journal_recovery.cpp, one source file built by examples/CMakeLists.txt as journal_recovery and run by tests/run_tests.sh. The comment at the top of the file describes each step. Back to the example programs.
